analysis.title: GS Morning: 1) US Midterms Recap, 2) BoE Preview, 3) Latam CB Round-Up, 4) USDJPY as an AI Hedge and 5) CNY Update (5 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Alec Phillips expects Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs and reverse last year's spending cuts. The first test is December 11, when spending authority expires. A short-term extension to February or March is the most likely outcome.

GS expects Democrats to reverse last year's spending cuts, which would add about 0.25% of GDP to spending in 2027. A deal on discretionary spending or expanded health insurance subsidies would add modestly to that.

Democratic wins at the state and local level are likely to bring short-term data centre moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data centre capacity expansion. GS expects the issue to fade and the moratoria to be short-lived.

GS Europe Economics (Stehn) expects the BoE to vote 7-2 for a 25bp hike, citing higher energy prices, upside activity surprises and an improving labour market. GS now expects a second hike to 4.25% Bank Rate in February.

GS Economics thinks market pricing of over 100bp of BoE tightening over the next year is too high, because second-round effects into wages look contained and consumer spending growth is likely to slow over the winter.

GS STIR trading (Daryl Li) says Nov-Mar MPC pricing is a cumulative 36bps, down from 41bps the day before. Li thinks pricing should be 0-1 hikes per quarter, not 1-2, and sees more to come out with or without de-escalation.

Li does not expect an outsized reaction to a 7-2 vote or an 8-1 vote. A 6-3 vote would take more out of December pricing. With the war unresolved, receiving December is a short vol trade that probably can only get down to about 4bps. A re-escalation with gas towards 120+ would be needed to put a December hike truly on the table.

Brazil's BCB left Selic unchanged at 13.75% after five consecutive 25bp cuts. The decision was unanimous and in line with market pricing (78.5% probability priced). GS expects a relief move in the rates curve, mostly flattening in longer tenors.

GS Economics expects Banxico to hold at 6.50% on the hawkish external backdrop (Fed hikes, global tightening, stronger USD, higher core yields, much higher oil) but gives a 40% probability to a split decision for a 25bp cut, as three of five directors lean dovish.

GS Trading expects a Banxico cut, pointing to dovish September minutes in which three of five directors were open to a cut. GS Trading also thinks Banxico's tolerance for MXN has shifted, with an 18-handle more acceptable and the discomfort now being a return to a 16-handle rather than a 19-handle.
GS FX Strats (Rastogi) calls short USDJPY the best FX hedge against an AI-trade drawdown, particularly as implied correlation for equities down / yields down has already repriced aggressively.
In the 20 largest twin drawdowns (equities and rates falling together) since 2000, the JPY cluster stands out as the preferred long, and JPY also stands out against USD.
USDJPY beta to 10y SOFR in historical twin drawdowns is about 12%. Mapping the 10th-percentile SOFR outcome into USDJPY gives a level the FX options market prices at only about 8% probability.

GS EM Strats (Sun Lu) reports from Beijing that expectations of large stimulus remain low, with YTD GDP growth within the 4.5-5% target range. More domestic demand-side policy is possible if exports decelerate meaningfully next year.

Beijing clients expect the official fiscal deficit to stay around 4% or rise to 4-4.5% over the next few years. The special local government bond quota may not rise in 2027 because of idle proceeds from this year's issuance.

Clients expect a stable US-China relationship near term, with leader meetings scheduled at APEC (Nov 18-19) and the G20 (Dec 14-15). Some expect deterioration in non-tariff areas such as finance and tech in 2027.

Clients expect gradual, trade-surplus-driven RMB appreciation to continue. Many said breaking 6.0 seems too early to conclude. PBoC wants exporters to hedge more and sell USD, and wants to avoid panic and excessively one-sided FX moves.

GS sees the recent 2% hike in the foreign currency deposit RRR as a symbolic move to slow the pace of RMB appreciation. GS sees a USDCNH downside entry once the spot-fixing gap narrows back to 200-300 pips, absent an external shock such as Middle East escalation.

GS expects seasonal exporter repatriation in December of at least US$70bn above average, likely pushing USDCNH to the 6.55-6.57 area by end of January. GS likes a 3-month USDCNH binary put targeting 6.55-6.57.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: energy prices are up, activity data surprised to the upside, the labour market is improving and the Governor and Deputy Governors signal openness to tightening. GS Economics expects a hike now and another in February, and market pricing is over 100bp over the next year.
tension_points.bear_case: Second-round effects into wages look contained and consumer spending growth is likely to slow over the winter. GS thinks the over-100bp pricing is too high, and GS STIR trading says data have been good but not exponential.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A re-escalation of the war with gas pushing towards 120+ would put a December MPC hike truly on the table.

tension_points.bull_case: Dovish case: three of five directors were open to a cut in September, with little walked back. GS Economics gives 40% to a split decision for a 25bp cut and GS Trading expects a cut.
tension_points.bear_case: Hawkish case: Fed hikes, global tightening, a stronger USD and weaker MXN, higher core yields and substantially higher oil argue for a hold at 6.50%, which is the GS Economics base case.
